why_this_exists: A scanned ORCHESTRAL score, which the other two precision corpora are not:
the hand-read Nottebohm page is vocal-clef counterpoint and the piano and
reference sheets are clean LilyPond engraving. A change that grouped header
ink vertically passed all three and still took treble clefs apart at the
waist here, reading seventeen of them as alto clefs. A thick scanned G clef
fragments in ways a clean engraving never does, so nothing else catches it.
This is a SPOT CHECK, not ground truth for the page. The staves listed are
the ones some version of the locator has read, checked by eye afterwards —
so it can catch a regression on them and says nothing about the rest. It is

staves.note: treble — read as alto by the unrestricted vertical rule
treble — read as mezzosoprano by the unrestricted vertical rule
narrow box, aspect 0.32 — a gate at 0.42 rejects this real clef
treble, read as soprano — main does this too, so it is the baseline rather than a regression
height 4.55 — a cap at 4.5 rejects this real clef
a real viola clef the current tolerance misses; it is read at 0.6 and lost at 1.0, which is part of what 1.0 costs
